references.text: Phinehas, son of Eleazar, showed his zeal for the Lord by stopping the plague in Israel, demonstrating his role as a defender of the covenant.
Phinehas was sent out as a priest in war, showing his leadership role among the priests in important national matters.
The Israelites feared that the altar would lead to unfaithfulness toward the Lord, as happened at Peor and with Achan's sin.
Unfaithfulness (ma'al) toward the Lord at Baal-Peor brought God's wrath, and Phinehas now declares that the tribes have not committed such unfaithfulness.
Achan's unfaithfulness (ma'al) toward the Lord brought wrath upon all Israel, which is the background for the concern in this chapter.
The promise that the Lord will be among his people when they keep the covenant confirms Phinehas' words that the Lord is in their midst.
The Lord dwells among his people, and his wrath can flare up over unfaithfulness—a theme underlying Phinehas' joy that the tribes are innocent.
